briefing.text: 'Piano' is one value of the SCNA_CLUSTER column in data_clinical_sample.txt; the other values are Mezzo-forte and Forte (the library counted Piano 115, Mezzo-forte 70, Forte 47 of 232 whole-genome-sequenced lung cancers in never smokers). The hypothesis is therefore about this study's own cohort and variables. Tabulate SCNA_CLUSTER yourself to confirm the group sizes before comparing mutational burden across clusters.
briefing.reason: Without knowing Piano is a column value in these tables, a team could wrongly treat the hypothesis as outside the data and answer Not verifiable.

briefing.text: 'High mutational burden' is a relative claim, so do not judge Piano's TMB on its own or from its median alone. Compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS between Piano and each of the other SCNA clusters, and as a check recompute per-sample mutation counts from data_mutations.txt. TMB is skewed, so use Kruskal-Wallis plus pairwise Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney tests, and report medians and the direction of each difference. Base the decision on whether Piano is higher than, similar to, or lower than the other clusters.
briefing.reason: This sets the comparison and the statistical test; judging the median of one group alone could lead to the wrong call.

briefing.text: An absolute TMB-high threshold commonly used in the clinic is >=10 mutations/Mb (e.g. FDA 2020 tissue-agnostic pembrolizumab approval, FoundationOne CDx). As a secondary view, report the fraction of each SCNA cluster above this threshold, alongside the relative comparison between clusters.
briefing.reason: 'High' can mean either relative or absolute burden; checking both keeps the conclusion from depending on one reading.

briefing.text: Histology can confound burden comparisons between copy-number clusters: carcinoids are a distinct histology with low TMB and quiet copy number and are often excluded or analysed separately. Check histology and tumour purity by cluster, and rerun the cluster comparison within adenocarcinomas and/or adjusted for purity to see whether the direction holds. (Background knowledge only; not verified against sources.)
briefing.reason: Composition by histology or purity could create or hide a difference in TMB between clusters, so a sensitivity analysis is needed.

shared_assumptions: Both teams read 'high mutational burden' as Piano being higher than the other SCNA clusters, and used TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS (nonsynonymous per Mb) as the measure of burden.

Both teams treated the SCNA_CLUSTER labels as fixed and complete. Neither reported how many samples have a blank cluster or a cluster with an unusual spelling, or whether leaving those out could matter.

Both teams assumed that the per-sample counts in data_mutations.txt cover the whole genome, so they can stand in for burden. It is not shown that the file is not filtered, for example to coding or driver variants only.
unused_evidence: MUTS_SUBCLONAL_RATIO: subclonality bears on how 'burden' is read (clonal vs total), and only team B looked at its median.
HLA_LOH, PASSIVE_SMOKING, TISSUE_SOURCE_SITE and the SV table (it holds an SCNA_Cluster column). These are unlikely to reverse the direction, but site or batch could confound TMB.

The genome-wide (all-variant) mutation count from data_mutations.txt, as opposed to nonsynonymous TMB only. Team B checked that the two agree, but neither team reported a by-cluster comparison of total SNV plus indel burden.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: no cluster reaches the absolute high-TMB cutoff, so 'high' can only be read in relative terms. Team A reported this but did not resolve it. Here it leads to the same label either way, because Piano is the lowest cluster.
Team B: no purity-adjusted model. Team A did fit one, which partly covers this.
second_readings: 'High mutational burden' could mean high in absolute terms (for example at least 10 mut/Mb), not higher than the other clusters. Under both readings Piano would not be 'high', so the label does not depend on which reading is used.
Burden could mean total genome-wide SNVs and indels, not nonsynonymous TMB. This needs a check that the direction is the same.
challenge.verdict: I trust the agreed answer (Piano has lower, not higher, burden, so the label is False) highly. Two teams found the same direction by different routes, and it held up after restricting to adenocarcinomas and after histology and purity adjustment. The remaining questions are robustness checks that are unlikely to reverse the direction.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: How many samples have a blank or non-standard SCNA_CLUSTER value? Does putting them aside, or setting them out as their own group, change the Piano-vs-others direction or your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Count all variants per sample in data_mutations.txt, including non-coding, synonymous and indels, not only nonsynonymous ones. Is Piano still the lowest cluster on that total-burden measure, and does the result change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Fit a model of log TMB with SCNA cluster plus histology, tumour purity and tissue source site. Does Piano remain lower once site and purity are held fixed, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Compare clonal-only mutation burden (TMB multiplied by 1 minus MUTS_SUBCLONAL_RATIO) across SCNA clusters. Does Piano's relative position change, and does that change your method?
